[h2]Insurgency: Sandstorm Review[/h2]

[h1]This Is Not Like CS:GO[/h1]
I always wanted to try Insurgency: Sandstorm and I am glad I finally got the opportunity to play it. From just seeing the game’s trailer and a few gameplay videos, I thought it’d be similar to games like CS:GO and Valorant which I am familiar with since I play them a lot. Well, I was wrong. This game’s concept might be a bit similar but gameplay-wise, it’s nowhere close to those. It was a very bumpy start.

This game is actually a sequel to “Insurgency”. Although I have owned the game since forever, I never played it. I might give it a shot after playing this game for a bit! But from the looks of it, this game looks like a huge upgrade from its prequel.

[h1]About This Game [/h1]

[h2]Storyline [/h2]
When I was researching about this game, I found out that the developers actually planned on making a single-player story campaign the main game mode. But they had to cancel it since it was considered “Sensitive” as the game was supposed to be set in the Middle East. As a result of this, the game has no lore of any sort. I wish they had just changed the premise of the game to a fictional place instead of completely dropping the idea. After seeing how amazing the overall gameplay mechanics are, a single-player campaign would’ve felt amazing to play.

[h2]Gameplay[/h2]
Insurgency: Sandstorm is a bit heavy when it comes to gameplay mechanics. This is mostly because the game is a bit too realistic. So, here are the mechanics:

[b]Movement[/b]
The movement mechanics used here can be found in many FPS games. You have usual walking, running, jumping, crouching, going prone, sliding, vaulting, and leaning. Everything feels slower than usual due to the game leaning toward the realistic side. But once you get used to it and master movement, combining all these different mechanics will play a pivotal role in anything you try to do.

[b]Loadouts & Weapons[/b]
In this game, you get to choose from 8 different loadouts to play as. Each of these comes with its own unique weapon choices. Sadly, you need to unlock these kits by leveling up. These are the different loadouts:
[olist]
[*] Rifleman
[*] Breacher
[*] Advisor
[*] Demolitions
[*] Marksman
[*] Gunner
[*] Observer
[*] Commander 
[/olist]

These kits apply for the Versus and Co-Op game modes. The Dominations game mode has only 5 of these as follows; Assaulter, Advisor, Breacher, Gunner, and Marksman. Then the Survival mode has only the Survivor loadout.

Inside each of these loadouts, you can customize a lot of things. You can change the Primary Weapon, Secondary weapon, Explosives 1-3 (The number of explosives you can carry depends on the class you choose), how much ammo to carry, what type of armor and accessory. In addition to these, you can get specific attachments for each weapon you carry. But yes, there is a catch. There is a limit to how much you can customize. There’s some kind of points thing for each class and each customization costs a certain number of these points. So yeah, unfortunately, you can’t customize to your heart’s content or it will make the game a bit broken. The game is indeed rich when it comes to loadout and weapon customization!

So, how do the weapons feel? Bro, it took me a while to get used to shooting in this game. Ads firing is nowhere close to what CS and Val have. You’re seldom fully accurate due to weapon sway, your character breathing, and other factors. All these mechanics implemented to make weapons feel realistic, add a lot to the game’s challenge factor. The most unique mechanic is the “Fast Reload” which happens when you press the Reload keybind twice. Upon doing this, your character throws away the current magazine even if it has some ammo left, and reloads a new magazine. This can be used to reload faster but you have to sacrifice some rounds and ammo conservation is pretty important in this game. But I do prefer the unrealistic shooting CS: GO has.

[b]Game Modes[/b]
As mentioned earlier, this game was supposed to have a single-player story mode but they canceled that idea. As a result of that, this game is now a purely multiplayer experience. So, there are three major game modes that have a few sub-modes as follows:

~Online Play~
Under online play, there are three significant modes namely Co-Op, Versus, and Community Servers.
[i]Co-op comprises of:[/i]
[olist]
[*] Checkpoint
[*] Hardcore Checkpoint
[*] Outpost
[*] Survival
[/olist]
[i]Versus comprises of:[/i]
[olist]
[*] Push
[*] Firefight
[*] Frontline
[*] Domination
[*] Ambush
[*] Time-specific modes. For example, at the time I wrote this review, there is this limited mode named “Night Battle” where the match takes place at night time and you have access to night gear. 
[/olist]
[i]And finally, Community Servers:[/i]
[olist]
[*] You can basically join community-created servers which may either be vanilla or modded. 
[/olist]

~Local Play~
As the name suggests, this is for playing a match with/against your squad. Basically, you can make a custom match. You can customize the time of the day, the map you want to play in, and choose from 4 scenarios. You can also use this mode to practice against bots since the game auto-fills the empty spaces with bots. Trust me, bots actually play well!

~Tutorials~
This is the last major game mode available. Inside this mode, you can choose from 3 sub-modes; Basic Training, Range(You can choose day or night before going into the range), and Lessons. This mode is important for honing your in-game skills!

[b]DLCs[/b]
Surprisingly enough, this game has a shit tonne of DLCs. All of them are literally just cosmetics. If you want to waste money on making your character and weapons look better, then be my guest. You do not require cosmetics to play the game better or anything, so try not to fall for the temptation of buying skins. I will not be listing them since it’s just a waste of time and space so [url=https://store.steampowered.com/dlc/581320/Insurgency_Sandstorm/]click here[/url] to see all of the downloadable content this game offers!

[h2]Visuals and Sound[/h2]
The game actually has amazing visuals. All assets used are made with the intention to give the player an immersive experience of a battlefield. I really loved the weapons’ animations. They’re really good omg! The aural aspect of the game is also perfect. I don’t know how to explain but just know that this segment of the game is perfect!

[h1]Pros[/h1]
[list]
[*] The game’s mechanics are pretty realistic and surprisingly smooth.
[*] Since it’s purely a multiplayer game, it has a very high replayability rate. 
[*] The visual and aural aspect of the game is amazing.
[*] The game’s player base is still active and they still release new updates along with new events.
[*] You have access to a huge collection of weaponry and equipment.
[*] Most of the guns can be customized. 
[*] There’s a decent amount of game modes. There’s even a game mode where you can play with and against actually decent bots to practice.
[/list]

[h1]Cons[/h1]
[list]
[*] Why did they completely cancel the single-player story mode! :(
[*] The community is a bit too toxic and not beginner friendly. So yeah, be careful when you join a match as a new player.
[/list]

[h1]Conclusion[/h1]
Playing this game for the first time was more of a challenge than fun. It took me a few matches just to get a grip on the game’s mechanics. I have not yet mastered anything and still rely on the “Spray ‘n Pray” technique. If you invest enough hours into this game and maybe even recruit a squad to play with you, you will surely enjoy this game more! Is it worth its price? Seeing the game’s quality, I would say it’s worth the price. But on the other hand, it’s a purely multiplayer game, and having such a huge price tag just means that the player base would be small.

Rating: 9/10

Ever since I played [i]Insurgency 2014[/i], I’ve never seen anything quite like it in terms of immersion, intense close quarters combat, and satisfying gunplay. So when I heard there was a sequel in the works, I was interested to see how it turns out. And after months of playing the Alpha and Beta phases, the game is now finally released.

[h1]Gameplay[/h1]
[i]Insurgency: Sandstorm[/i] at its heart is a fast-paced tactical shooter. In order for the game to feel immersive, the HUD is minimalistic, and crosshairs are nowhere to be found. Firearms are a real threat and a couple of shots are enough to drop the enemies. For this reason, the gunplay is extremely satisfying. On top of that, an extensive arsenal of weapons is available to players to choose from. Currently, [i]Sandstorm[/i] offers a Co-op mode vs bots and three PvP modes for small and large battles, with more content planned to be added after the launch. Other new additions include bigger maps, fire support, and vehicles.

[h1]Visuals and Sound[/h1]
The game looks very good, and weapons have been modeled with extreme attention to detail. Maps are now considerably bigger, and the added detail makes them more believable. There is a broad range of customizations available for the characters and seldom do they look similar. However, character models look lifeless, and their moving animations feel off.
When it comes to sound design, [i]Sandstorm[/i] truly shines. The Arabic accent of the Insurgents is superbly done. The explosions are deafening and powerful weapon sounds contribute to the enjoyment of gunplay. Further, gunshots sound different depending on the shooter’s position. [i]Sandstorm[/i] is the kind of game that needs to be played with a good pair of headphones.

[h1]Performance[/h1]
The game’s performance has improved considerably since the start of the Beta phase, but it’s still nowhere as smooth as its predecessor. Overall, its optimization leaves a lot to be desired. While the game runs fine most of the time, occasional hiccups and frame drops are to be expected. Moreover, in my time with the game, I’ve witnessed all manners of bugs and glitches. Hopefully, given time, most of these issues will be patched.

[h1]Verdict[/h1]
As much as I enjoyed [i]Insurgency: Sandstorm[/i], It’s not a game for everyone. Playing it requires a bit of time, patience, teamwork and strategy and is aimed towards more mature players. As a long-time [i]Insurgency[/i] fan, I was hyped for [i]Sandstorm[/i] and the final product does not disappoint. I highly recommend checking the game out if you are interested in tactical shooters.

This game is mostly great. However, it has a few setbacks, and unfortunately, I can no longer recommend the game.

PROS:
- Fun core gameplay. Guns and movement feel great and balanced. Time to kill is low (1 to 2 bullets from any gun can kill at most ranges) and punishment for death is moderate so it forces you to play a bit more cautious than most shooters, and think before you act.
- Communication is great. It is awesome to join a full game with great teammates who communicate and crack jokes. You can hear the other team in proximity during game and between rounds, so it can make for some fun conversation and hilarious moments.
- The atmosphere is casual. In-fact, competitive mode is completely dead, so you will not find sweaty players here. Toxicity levels therefore are quite low compared to most shooters.

CONS:
- As stated in other reviews, every time this game goes on sale, there is an influx of cheaters. After 360 hours, it becomes quite obvious who cheats (low levels who outperform all others and one tap you from angles that don't exist). This is a serious problem that I don't think a small studio is equipped to handle, or worse, turns a blind eye in favor of $$.
- There is a subset of players who are all > lvl. 1000. These players always queue together and when they join your game, they ruin it for everyone. They know all the most extreme and cheesy angles and abuse them and it turns a good time into an awful one. Because the player base is so small (~3000 online at a given time) you will run into these clowns and it WILL ruin it for you.
- The automatic team balancing is awful and illogical. It will auto-balance you back and forth between teams in a single match. It will not transfer enough team members to the other team (or nobody at all) leaving one team still with a large deficit. It also does not take into account player level nor skill, so one team will have a ton of high levels and the other full of scrubs to get farmed.
- The barrier to entry for newcomers is quite high. As a new player, you WILL think everyone around you is cheating because you get 1 tapped from outer space. It takes several hours of getting used to the the maps and the style of play before you will start to perform at an average level, even for seasoned FPS players.
- The rate of development is quite slow. They release a new map and a new gun every so often, but it gets dull quick. They could iterate on the game much quicker to release more new and exciting content, but they either do not have the capability or willingness to do so.

2019 REVIEW:

Right so here is my humble opinion on Insurgency Sandstorm.  I am an old school gamer and have been around since Atari days.  Through the years I have played MANY shooters including the usual suspects like COD or BF.  What follows is my take on the game and based on my system (Ryzen 5 2600, GTX1060-6GB and 16GB Vengeance 3000mhz).  

I am aware that some folks report issues with frame rates etc, but I must make it perfectly clear that I have no issues with frame rates and performance other than in PVP where there certainly is an issue or two with lag.

This game is brutal and I say brutal in the most loving way ever.  I played a fair bit of the original Insurgency and this is tougher than that.  To me that is beautifully brutal and just what we needed.  For any newcomers or those considering to buy this game, please remember the following…………this game is hard, but easily the best in terms of creating a feeling of reward and satisfaction to the player.  Every bullet can kill!  Once you get that and realise that you cannot run and gun this game like your average arcade shooter (COD or BF) then you start to see the beauty I am referring to.

No-one in this game cares about how many kills you have.  Team work is the only thing that matters.  If a quick fix for KD is what you want then this game is NOT for you.  If you want to feel epic for actually getting a kill THAT counted or taking an objective to get your whole team back in, then THIS is the game for you. 

It is only natural for some to try and compare it to other titles.  I will make it simple.  Sandstorm is a shooter and that is about all it has in common with any other shooter out there.  This is a tactical game where accuracy and good decision making and communication is rewarded (I must stress this again, no-one cares how many kills you have!!! I really mean that!!).  If you want to  impress then start playing the game the way it was meant to be played……RULE 1 – always play the objective!  RULE 2 – you are not John Rambo! RULE 3 – you are great only if you as a team (not glory hunters, who end up dead most the time) succeed in winning a round, not because of your own KD.  Again I cannot stress of how little importance KD is in this game.  Look at the leader board when you are playing, more often than not high kills amount to nothing in terms of personal gain XP.  You want XP?  Then capture that objective and hold it as potentially the last man in the team to be a hero!  That is how you make friends in Sandstorm.  

This game will give you a feeling of reward you have never experienced before.  True we only have only 6 maps at the moment, but you know, this is New World we are dealing with.  If you knew anything about them then you would know that like the first one this game is going to be an epic masterpiece.

I strongly recommend this to anyone who are up for a proper challenge and sick of the same old KD driven games out there.  This game is honest and brutal, that is EPIC!

Normally I'd play a game for close to a hundred hours or so on a game that's got little nuances and small details before I write a review but this time it has to be done. If any of the developers stumble upon this, I humbly request you read this through to the end.

EDIT: I wrote this review at about 30 hours in, I now have over a hundred hours more in the game. I am quite enjoying it.

PROS

1) Shooting mechanics are really good. The recoil is like a real firearm would be, maybe a bit overdone from my experience but I'm no firearms expert and I haven't used some of the weapons featured in this game
2) It is quite tactical, and you have to think when you play. You can also run and gun, be aggressive and pile as much pressure as possible on the opposition, if that's your playstyle it's a totally viable strategy, but expect to be punished a lot if you're new to this style of game
3) The sound engineering is top notch. Seriously, this game is a stunning example of what good sound is in a video game, the sound staging is amazing and individual weapon sounds are EXCELLENT. If any developer wants to take something positive from this game, then this is a contender. To those who did the sound engineering, if you've read this, I salute you and raise a toast to you.
4) The tension..... You can be on the edge of your seat straining your ears for any sounds, being the last one alive knowing that you're being hunted down like a mad dog, knowing that if you're discovered a swift execution possibly awaits you
5) It has a rather steep learning curve, forcing you to learn the game and, to some extent, some basic knowledge of firears such as differences in weapon calibers. 
6) Realistic kills. No more putting 10 rounds in a guys back only for him to turn around and blow your head off. Sometimes a couple shots is all you need, hell sometimes it's just the one shot
7) The UI is brilliant, very unobtrusive. They also added a little bit to show you amo counts. They've kept the cycling system which I highly appreciate
8) This game looks beautiful thanks to UE4, but from its move from Source there's a huge CON.
9) OFFLINE BOTS! And these bots are much much better than you'd expect.
10) Maps are much much larger now, but again there's a CON to this,
11) They included one technical vehicle, which can be used to DEVASTATING effect
12) Improvements in mechanics,such as the speed reload (I love this), the staged reload system (really intelligent) and the inclusion of the Commander and Observer roles from their past title, Day of Infamy
13) No paid DLC, all post launch content will be free (if I'm not mistaken)
UPDATE: Looks like there will be cosmetic microtransactions?
UPDATE 2: Yes there have been cosmetic microtransactions, so far I am OK with that as they do not have any effect to gameplay or pay to win aspects (unless maybe the new snow camo works well on snow maps? Not sure)
14)Mod support. But it is not implemented via the Steam Workshop. Mods are from mod.io because even consoles can have mods then, which, while I appreciate the mod support, Steam workshop would have been a much much better choice.
UPDATE:
15)Switchable optics? Yes please. That really changes how you would play the game, switching from a 2x scope in midrange to a 1x in CQC engagements is amazing! Thank you NWI!


CONS:
1) BUGS AND PERFORMANCE ISSUES!!! That's what mainly made me write this review, the performance issues are crazy. Frame drops for some people are mad, for example I sometimes get frame drops to 20 in firefights (given I have a GTX 965m, I know that my GPU is limiting)
UPDATE: I changed my system (R5 2600 16G 3200 and a 1070 at 2560x1080), and now it runs a lot better, but I still get some performance issues (rarely though, it feels much better now)
UPDATE 2: Well this game initially ran horribly on my friends rig(R5 3600, 5700XT, 64GB DDR4 3600, game on SSD) for a long while but finally we have it running a lot better at high details at 21:9 1080p, optimisation is a lot better now!
UPDATE 3: I am running the game just fine on my rig, and it's on a HDD. FPS lock at 90 and it is doing quite well! Sadly I can't get RTSS to lock it at 75 (I have a 75Hz panel), but 90 is great too. 

2) GAME BREAKING EXPLOITS!!!! The increased map size leads to some exploits, and some of the map design isn't that great. Push sometimes can end up becoming just spawn camping, which is just sad and no longer any fun. Not to mention some people breaking the game to insane levels in maps. Look at this video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mdQc5EuCAXc ..... Note I do not suggest nor do I encourage you to do this stuff, but please do look at what's possible (And frankly I'm not really going to weigh in on the ban he has and what have you, both sides have a point and I'll leave it at that.)
3) People I know personally just can't handle the recoil and don't understand it
UPDATE: Some updates have reduced the amount of recoil by quite a bit.

4) Steep learning curve (Listed as a pro but some people can't handle it)
UPDATE: The game is a lot more accessible now for people!
5) Updates do take a while, but that is probably because the developers want to push a polished update.
6) Steam workshop and mod support has not been implemented yet, and that's what kept the previous game so refreshing 
UPDATE: this point has been addressed

7) This con cannot be the fault of the developers, but it needs to be said. Some of the community are downright horrible. Trolling in game, voice chat spam after a match can be the same as Insurgency 2014s too. Although, the servers I frequent usually have disciplined people playing it so you don't get the voice spam or the obnoxious trolling

Insurgency : Sandstorm is an incredible shooter, and I can happily recommend this game to anyone interested in the genre. As of writing this review, I have over 160 hours in the game, with 159 of them being in the "PvE" modes. This will be the main focus of my review.

What makes this game so great in my eyes? To me, it strikes the perfect balance of tactical and arcade shooter. The shooting and gunplay is hands down some of the greatest I've ever seen and felt in a video game. Since you will primarily be shooting other people, they HAD to get this right. They nailed it. Guns feel weighty, sound incredible, and the death reactions are almost hauntingly realistic at times. This game employs active ragdoll physics, and it's tough going to other shooters expecting the enemies to drop the way they do here. The best comparison I can make is Rockstar's "Euphoria" engine, just not quite as robust.

Weapon selection is really solid. Certain weapons are kept to specific classes to maintain a sense of balance. In order to use sniper rifles, you must choose the "Marksman" class for example. But make no mistake, even the basic Rifleman class (which has no limit) can be effective at all ranges with the right setup. Breacher is my favorite class, as using the shotgun is insanely satisfying.

Loadouts use a point and weight system. Certain weapons, attachments, and accessories cost more points than others. I have found almost any weapon to be viable, as most guns will instantly kill an enemy with a torso or headshot. Death in this game happens quickly, and it can take some getting used to. The AI does feel a little cheap at times, but those moments are pretty rare and keep you on your toes.

Character customization! As you level up, you unlock credits which can be used to purchase cosmetics. This allows you to separate yourself from others in terms of appearance. I have also found that each time you level up, you also unlock a new piece of gear to wear. This can be anything from hats to pants to camo patterns. This is a really cool mechanic, and building a unique character is a lot of fun. Only downside is no weapon camos without buying the skins with real money. 

This ties in to one of my biggest flaws with the game : Progression. After a while, it can kind of feel redundant simply unlocking more cosmetics. Most of what you will use in the game is unlocked right when you begin playing. I believe this was done by design, as I can't help but think they were competing with Counter Strike to become a more streamlined, intense shooter. None of this really matters though, as the game itself is solid enough that I don't mind not unlocking more things to use other than basic cosmetics.  

The community is overall non-toxic, and I very rarely encounter griefers in the PvE gamemodes. Cheating is also a non-issue from what I have seen. Maps are overall really good, with only a couple that I generally do not enjoy playing. But the game does have map voting, which is a great touch.

This is all in the base version of the game. The modded PvE servers are insanely fun as well, which a lot more variety and tougher enemies. I'm perfectly fine playing the base version of the game though.

Overall, I highly recommend picking this game up. It's intense for sure, but the gameplay is captivating and as of right now is the only one of it's kind in terms of PvE. Do yourself a favor and pick this up, you won't regret it ;)

After growing tired of Counter-Strike, Insurgency: Sandstorm has become my go-to online shooter. It strikes a near-perfect balance between tactical and arcade gameplay. The guns look and sound authentic, and shooting feels incredibly satisfying. While shooting skill is important, situational awareness and teamwork are even more critical. You could get just five kills in a match and still earn MVP if you focus on supporting your team, capturing objectives, and providing fire support.

On the downside, getting from spawn to the nearest objective can feel tedious, and the game introduces a significant element of randomness due to large maps with numerous rooms and hiding spots. It's impossible to control every situation on your own, so without good team coordination, failure is almost inevitable.

One standout feature is the proximity voice chat. If you're unsure whether there's an enemy in a room, you can say something provocative over the mic, like how you took his mom on a date - nine times out of ten, he'll react, giving away his presence.

Ok, so to start - This game runs badly on any CPU with only 4 cores. That puts you i5 owners out there in a pickle. I saw it for myself, my 4690k @ 4.4 ghz was constantly maxed out at 95-100% CPU usage, which led to lots of stuttering and dropped frames. I've since upgraded (not specifically for this game) to a humble r5 2600 and wow what a massive difference it made. No more CPU bottleneck. So there's that to consider before you buy this game, can your CPU run it sufficiently? 

With that said, I love this game. It's immersive, unforgiving and incredible fun. One minute you are in a long range gun battle down an alley way, the next your indoors seeing your buddies get blown to bits by a suicide bomber. I know this game is going to get better and better. As mentioned in other reviews, there are bugs, no disputing that. What game these days doesn't have bugs? (*cough BFV cough*) This isn't a AAA game with massive money behind it. The difference here is that the Devs have passion for this game and seem to love what they do, and it shows through. The game has soul and that's part of the reason I keep on coming back. The Devs are working hard to iron out issues, updates are coming fairly consistently. 

For the record, I'm running a mid range rig. Ryzen 2600 @4ghz, 16gb Ram @3200mhz and an RX 480 Nitro @ factory settings. 1080p at low settings with TAA, I get 100 - 140+ fps. At medium with Very high textures and TAA I get 70 - 100 fps, which is what I play at (I've got a 75hz monitor). The frames can jump around a bit as mentioned, so I cap mine at 90 and it sits there most of the time or use Vsync and it's a pretty solid 75 fps. Shadows seem to be the biggest hit on FPS for me, as going from low to medium introduces dynamic shadows, and cuts FPS by up to HALF depending on the scene. Lots of characters throwing shadows like in the truck at the start of a round drops from 120fps down to 70fps.

[h1] ♦️ Insurgency: Sandstorm [/h1]
[b] Insurgency: Sandstorm [/b] is the sequel to Insurgency which was a standalone game based off of the original which was a mod for Half life. It is an FPS that heavily focuses heavily on its simulation/immersive gameplay. Not to the extent of popular mil-sim shooters such as Arma and Squad but more of a middle ground between Battlefield and Squad. Sandstorm which has been a controversial topic among the community, still manages to carve out its own loyal playerbase, but is it worth a play?

[h1] Loadouts [/h1]
→ One of Sandstorms biggest features is the vast array of weapons at your disposal. They are all modeled beautifully with tons of attention to detail! And it sure doesn’t disappoint creating a loadout has never been better, instead of limiting your options due to what the game designers say you can bring you will be prioritizing what's most important to you. You are given twenty tokens that you can spend on different guns, attachments, light/heavy armor, grenades, and more! Towards finalizing your loadout you will make tough decisions deciding between more ammo, heavier armor, or those sweet sweet attachments. 
 → I’ve noticed when playing that people tend to have drastically different loadouts compared to another or even my own. It seems this loadout system has done its best to combat the biggest problem in modern FPS’s, meta weapons. Gone are the CoD4 days of everyone running the M16, even in CoD:MW the M4A1 was a popular choice. With such a short TTK it means almost every weapon is viable, so don’t be afraid to experiment with your weapon choices! 

[h1] Gunplay [/h1]
→ Easily the greatest aspect of Sandstorm is how the guns feel and how fights play out. It does its best to stay ‘realistic’ where every gun can be lethal if you hit your shots! Most ARs are 1-3 body shots for a kill, snipers 1 shot, etc. this creates such a unique playstyle that you must adjust too. This creates a slower playstyle that most adopt where holding angles and having teammates around are critical for survival. But when I say slow I don't mean the snail pace of most mil-sim shooters, but again a middle ground between arcade and simulation. 
https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2345972091

[h1] Player Vs. Environment [/h1]
→ Not a fan of PvP? No problem, Sandstorm also features a co-op or solo mode that allows you to fight near endless bots. There are even three unique game modes to enjoy checkpoint, operation, and outpost. This can be another great way to enjoy the many systems of Sandstorm without the intense atmosphere of PvP. Personally I wasn’t the biggest fan of PvE, but I certainly appreciate the addition of PvE in Sandstorm. Now my opinion on this isn’t widely accepted, there is a community of dedicated players that solely enjoy PvE if that is your style.

[h1] Player Vs. Player [/h1]
→ Now for the main attraction, PvP. With four different game modes being push, firefight, capture the base, and skirmish. They also included more arcade game modes such as team deathmatch and domination. PvP is really a joy to play, as you experiment with different loadouts while engaging in thrilling fights with gunplay like no other game. It leads to firefights like unrivaled by the likes of Battlefield/CoD. 
→ Instead of these linear ‘lane’ fights you tend to see nowadays, the maps allow for holding strong locations and many opportunities to flank. This leads to team deathmatch not feeling like mindless killing until the score has been reached, but instead it feels like battles in a real war. There is lots of strategy to be played here to get the upper hand on your enemies, and playing like rambo is detrimental to your team.
https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2360036346

[h1] Visuals & Sound [/h1]
→ The visuals in Sandstorm are honestly pretty impressive with beautiful open maps, with attention to detail. It really helps give off the feeling of realism when the game almost (...almost) looks real. I enjoyed playing with minimal hud to see even more of the beauty that is Insurgency: Sandstorm. The lighting, textures, effects all tie together to create beautiful situations in battle or even lovely vistas when the action is slow.
→ The guns here sound amazing almost 1:1 with their real life counterparts for most weapons. AR sounds mean and deadly, the boom of sniper shots in the distance are all done amazingly. My only gripe is the poor locational footsteps sounds, I feel like no game nowadays can accurately tell me where enemies are solely on sound alone. This isn’t a Sandstorm problem as much as it's a genre problem. Apex, RB6, Warzone all do such a horrible job at footstep and sadly Sandstorm isn’t breaking the cycle in that regard. 
https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2360036054

[h1] ♦️ Conclusion [/h1]
Overall Insurgency: Sandstorm is great at what it is trying to do, offering a middle ground between arcade shooters and the mil-sim genre. With tons of loadout variations, exciting gunplay, short TTK making every match intense and immersive. Now do I think this can be your go to shooter for years to come? Maybe, but it can offer a fun experience that you can always hop in and out of!

[h1]PvE Multiplayer at its finest. [/h1]

Insurgency Sandstorm is a multiplayer FPS developed by New World Interactive, it’s the follow-up to Insurgency (2014). I don’t typically play or review multiplayer games, but I gave this a try during a free weekend recently and ended up buying it during the summer sale. This is the most fun I’ve had with a multiplayer game since the Halo franchise on my late Xbox 360. 

Two things to keep in mind when you read this review: I have only played PvE, and this review is almost exclusively about PvE. I play on the US East servers, so my comments about finding games may not apply to you.

[h1]Positives: [/h1]
[list][*]Insurgency Sandstorm looks great. The game looks fairly realistic and even on lower settings it still looks pretty good.

[*]The gunplay is excellent. All of the weapons are well designed, and different weapons definitely have a different feel to them, they all pack quite a punch. It’s fun messing around with different weapons to try and figure out which one suits your playstyle the best.

[*]The maps are well designed and I haven’t found them to get boring. I’m not entirely sure how many there are but it’s somewhere around five or six with more on the way at some point. There are different maps for security or insurgents too which helps add some variety.

[*]The PvE mode is just fantastic and for me fully justifies the purchase of the game. Essentially, you have a team of eight security or insurgent fighters going up against the enemy and trying to capture/complete certain objectives. All of the maps have between six and eight objectives that are either capture a point or detonate an explosives cache. Two or three of the capture points will also need to be defended for one to three minutes after the capture (always the final objective, but for the other ones it varies for each game). 

[*]PvE matches can take anywhere from fifteen to forty-five minutes depending on how many tries it takes you to get through all of the objectives. Most of my matches have lasted for thirty to thirty-five minutes, so they are a pretty decent length. I think for a co-op mode it works better to have matches a little bit longer, but obviously that means it’s not so great if you just want to pick it up for a quick match every once in a while.

[*]You start with all weapons, attachments and equipment unlocked, which makes a nice change. Instead of having to work to unlock things, you simply have a point-based allowance for what you can equip. This system works incredibly well and mitigates the issue of more experienced players having access to better equipment. The allowance is very fair. PvE mode has a slightly higher allowance than PvP does, I guess to help keep things a little more even in PvP.

[*]There are still unlocks, but they’re only cosmetic. Each time you level up you unlock new customization options for your security and insurgent character as well as 100 coins of in-game currency. The 100 coins feels a little stingy, but you should be able to do a fair amount of customization right off the bat or within a few levels. There are NO microtransactions!

[*]The way communication works is pretty neat. You have voice chat, text chat and a ping system. The voice chat is pretty cool because when you speak, people on both sides can hear you within a certain distance. It adds some extra risk/realism in both modes, and I thought it was a pretty neat feature. The text chat and ping system are both pretty standard. 

[*]The sound design is excellent. The weapons sound great, and you can really use sound to your advantage to hear when enemies are walking close by. The sound really helps create a feeling of immersion, especially if you’re using good quality headphones. 

[*]My experience with the community has been great so far. I haven’t encountered a single player who has been rude or any griefers. Most people will even apologize if they accidentally shoot you. 

[*]I’ve had no issue finding matches, I think the longest I’ve ever had to wait to find a match was about twenty seconds. For the most part you’ll join in at the start of a game but occasionally it’ll be mid-match. [/list]

[h1]Neutral: [/h1]
[list][*]While I’ve had no issue at all finding matches through the official servers, the community servers have seemed to be almost completely dead any time I’ve looked at the server browser. Not really sure how much of an issue this is, but I figured it was worth mentioning. [/list]

[h1]Negatives: [/h1]
[list][*]The game does have some performance issues. I’ve been lucky to not have it as bad as some, but the first match I play of any session is always plagued with issues such as my weapon (particularly my scope) not loading correctly and lots of stuttering/frame drops. How much of an issue performance is for you will depend heavily on what you’re playing it on. 

[*]There’s not much map variation in the official servers. Most of the PvE matches I join are on one of two maps, and there was one map that I saw for the first time ten hours into the game. I’d just like to see the other maps more. [/list]

[h1]Verdict: [/h1]

Insurgency Sandstorm offers the best PvE multiplayer experience I’ve had in a long time. Immersive sound, great gunplay and a surprisingly nice community. I typically don’t even like MP or FPS games, yet I absolutely love this one. I would consider this a must have for those who enjoy co-op shooters.

I'm an Insurgency veteran, having played it since its first release as a Half-Life 2 mod in 2007. I have also played the "second" title, which was released in 2014 as a standalone game on the newer Source engine. Insurgency is a tactical-based first person shooter that offers you a big amount of weapons, attachments, and character customization. The focus is primarily infantry, and so are the maps designed. Unlike the older titles, you have limited vehicle usage in this title (drivable technical car with a mounted machine gun on the back), and you can call in different air support like the Apache, Black Hawk, and A-10 airstrike. Every title that was released was also an improvement over the prior title. This title is still alive and kickin, matchmaking is pretty fast, it takes me max. 5 seconds to get into a match. You have hardcore realism gameplay, with no lifebar, no hitmarker, and every bullet can be deadly, unlike in games like Call of Duty and Battlefield. 

However, what I'm criticizing and what the previous insurgency titles (both from 2007 and 2014) did better are the map design and the factions. In the previous titles, there were many more urban maps, with great lighting and outskirts areas. Take a look at the Revolt map. You felt like it was a true Iraqi/Afghan area. There were Iraqi flags, Saddam Hussein graffiti, and Iraqi propaganda posters around the map, with Mercedes cars and different types of U.S. Vehicles placed around the maps.

The second thing are the factions: While in the very first title, you have USA vs Iraqi insurgents with their respective uniforms, in this title you have more common factions, Security vs Insurgents. So are the uniforms, which is a bit problematic. While it's great that you can customize your character (and you have ALOT of options), you have no more clear uniform identity. This means: You can make your security character look either like a common PMC or almost like an insurgent, and your insurgent character can be customized to look similar to a PMC. On the battlefield, it's confusing. I had to look twice, which sometimes killed me, and sometimes when I didn't look twice during battle, i killed a teammate.

However, I recommend this game over Call of Duty. It provides you realism and fun experience without the need to buy dozens of DLCs, unlike other shooters provided by AAA developers & publishers.

So i'm original insurgency veteran, around 900 hours, and there was a free week again and i decided to finally give this game a shot. But after a solid couple of hours the cracks started to show and I understood why most of the original insurgency playerbase never transitioned to this game. 

First let's address the performance, which to this day is not optimal. So from what I have read almost everyone even the guys with the high-end rigs have problems, myself included. Some areas this game runs without issues, 120fps on med to high no problems, as soon as there is a lot bullets or airstrikes or anything of that sort, this game struggles and it really doesn't matter that much what the settings are. This is super annoying since inconsistent framerate is even worse the consistent low framerate. That also leads to visibility issues which is to be expected with better graphics and good amount of custom clothing, but it is not that bad. 

Update: I did try out some of the solutions listed here and also on reddit and i have to say i was able to lock the game above 60fps at all time. So if you enjoy the game and the only problems are performance, you can totally get reasonable framerate if you dont mind screwing around with your game and pc settings. What was, at least for me far more annoying are the gameplay changes. So anyone that played the first insurgency knows how quickly you die in that game and it really did not matter what you were being shot with. Most guns two shot you, three shots at extreme long range if u were using low cal, the most extreme was the makarov pistol that could take up to five shots but it was a huge outlier in that regard. Simply put so long you had ap rounds and hitting center mass the targets would drop almost instantly. Here apart from shotguns you cannot change the weapons damage or penetration capabilities. And i'm not going to argue realism, but gameplay wise this makes some weapons extremely unfun to use, mainly the low cal fast firing ones. The reason being this game still has weapons that can one tap you at most common engagement distances, and also things like the uzi or mp5 which take waaaaaaaay too long get a kill. It just happened a bit too often where i run in to a situation where i have a drop on somebody, start firing first, hitting him multiple times and he just swings around and one taps me with FAL or some other high cal battle rifle. So basically despite there being a lot more weapons to chose from now, pretty much everyone goes for the highest caliber weapon you have in the class you are playing. Compared to the original, there also were weapons that were not as good as others, but it was never tied to the damage they did, if you hit someone first 99 times out of 100 you are going to win that fight. 

Other gameplay "features" that i just don't understand are the killcam which i think has no place in this game, but okay you want to make this game more friendly to non hardcore players, then why is the cam so bloody bad, the only thing it shows is a direction which u should already know, if you were paying attention when the hit indicators showed on your screen.

Vehicles which play such a small role i don't understand why even include them, like would it really break the game if they gave a respawn timer on the car on the push so you get more than 1 or in the case you 0 wave the first objective 2.

Speaking of cars, why are the mines in the game even, like i know for a fact they don't work this patch at all, but even if they did, the cars are so rare why even bother having them.

One gameplay feature that i have to praise here is the ammo management which is something i really missed in the original.

Map design is better in a sense that the maps are bigger and have way more cover and more paths to use but the distance to objective is far longer with far more restrictive red zones than there use to be, which i understand since spawnkilling was a big problem in the original, but for example precinct insurgent push delta point is so restrictive on the security side that they can't enter half of the buildings overlooking the objective, like that is a big overkill on the redzone in my opinion and it makes defending that very frustrating, also spawncamping still happens if you know where to do it, precinct security base being especially vulnerable to it.

Also the restrictive server setting which don't allow you to go spectator or switch teams, which i do get there used to be some issues with it in the original, but not having the option to switch to the weaker team to balance things out seems silly.

Also the official servers are not on the server browser so good luck trying to get the map you actually want to play, like honestly why not have them. I don't see a reason for that,

Finally the game overall polish..... which is garbage, how is this game out for over year and there is still soooooooo many bugs, glitches, gameplay issues, and overall lack of content, like holy crap if you compare this game to the original it does not stack well at all.
Coop, one mode, checkpoint with three variants, classic, hardcore and frenzy, the original, checkpoint, hunt, survival, outpost, conquer, all with classic, hardcore and elite options, which true don't change the dynamic as much as in sandstorm hardcore or frenzy but still overall a lot more options than we have here.

As for pvp, you have push, firefight, frontline and domination and the removed skirmish.

Poison gas is invisible most of the time.

Ranked system is so bare bones you will have no idea what actually matters (performance, 4v5 etc) in the game and what doesn't also work is the leaver buster which triggers even if you leave and reconnect late in to the 2 min prep phase, like wtf.

During the Alpha and Beta stages of Insurgency Sandstorm's development, the game showed quite a bit of potential. With maps twice as large as the original Insurgency, more intuitive gunplay, a fire support system, and driveable vehicles, Sandstorm brought a lot to the table. It excelled at creating an enjoyable middle ground between realistic and arcade type shooters that excelled in immersion. 

After release, development slowed down. Each update would bring new weapons, bug fixes, optimization. and occasionally a new map. The first few post-release maps were unfinished maps from the Alpha. As time went on, the new maps shifted from large scale battlegrounds to claustrophobic labyrinths of unconvincing ornately decorated mud houses, presumably for the purpose of pushing gameplay all into cqb. The new maps do an excellent job of providing no incentive at all to use the vehicles. They might as well not be in the game.

Each optimization pass had either little effect at all- or a negative effect. Many players who participated in the Alpha were unable to run the game after release. I find myself struggling to make 40 fps on the same settings I used to run the game at 60 on. Though impressive at high graphics settings, the game looks outright rancid at low detail settings. 

The original insurgency boasted a wide variety of game modes, both multiplayer and co-operative. There was something for everyone. Co-op had the casual and linear Checkpoint mode, stealth-oriented Hunt, tactical and coordination requiring Conquer, high-octane and terrifying Outpost, and more. PvP ranged from attack/defense to VIP escort to all out territorial skirmish. 

 Insurgency Sandstorm has 3 multiplayer and 2 co-op modes. After over 2 years, we've gained 2 game modes, and lost one. Rather than allowing users to choose their map, mode, playercount, and ping, NWI decided that  Sandstorm needed a matchmaking system. Whether out of their fabled "fear of splitting the playerbase" or arrogantly overestimating the size of their playerbase, we shall never know. Each server is locked to a specific game mode, and allows players to vote on the next map only. After installing counters that tells everyone how many people are playing each mode, a positive feedback loop led to Skirmish's playercount locking at zero. NWI thought the best course of action was to remove skirmish from the game. It was replaced by the very similar Frontline game mode, with the only difference between the two being that frontline is populated by massive blocks of "RESTRICTED AREA" that ensure that players are only allowed to stand at the 5% of the map closest to the current objective. Aside from silly modifications of Checkpoint, the only new co-op mode is a lobotomized version of Outpost, which attempts to make gameplay more rewarding by hurling waves of absolutely retarded AI soldiers armed nonsensical loadouts and by resetting the players to a new location on the map 3 times if everyone dies.

Once NWI got wind of the fact that they weren't making any more money, they decided to start doing something with the time we all thought they spent optimizing, and decided to start designing ridiculous DLC cosmetics to sell. Spirit Halloween skull masks, guns painted with red or blue, and most recently: militants dressed in decorative red and gold to celebrate the Chinese new year. What the fuck.

If you can look past the gerrymandered maps, shattered immersion, and poor optimization, the gameplay is still fine. But don't buy this game unless you'll be satisfied with no more than 3 practical game modes, and don't expect the updates to make the game any better. In fact, it's safest to assume that they'll make Sandstorm worse.

Edit: every new animation since the Cold Blood update have looked terrible, and they continue to add airsoft cosmetics

[b]Insurgency: Sandstorm is a tactical first-person shooter that has managed to carve its own niche in the realm of FPS games, offering a distinct and intense experience for players seeking a more realistic approach to combat.

[i]Pros:
Tactical Realism: Sandstorm shines in its realistic approach to combat. It emphasizes team-based tactics, effective communication, and thoughtful maneuvering over run-and-gun gameplay. The gunplay feels weighty and responsive, delivering an immersive and visceral experience.
Immersive Atmosphere: The game's attention to detail in sound design, visuals, and level design creates an immersive atmosphere that feels authentic and intense. From the realistic weapon handling to the tense urban environments, the game excels in immersing players in the battlefield.
Variety in Modes and Maps: Sandstorm offers diverse game modes such as Push, Firefight, and Co-op modes that add depth and variety to the gameplay. The maps are well-designed and provide a mix of open areas and tight urban spaces, offering different strategic opportunities.
Modding Support: The game's support for mods and community-created content extends its longevity. The modding community has created a range of custom maps, weapons, and other content, adding significant replayability.

Cons:
Learning Curve: The game's emphasis on realism and tactical gameplay can be daunting for newcomers. The learning curve, especially in terms of weapon handling and map awareness, might deter casual players seeking more accessible gameplay.
Technical Issues: While the game has seen improvements, occasional bugs, optimization issues, and server problems persist. This can lead to frustrating experiences, particularly during intense firefights or when joining matches.
Lack of Single-Player Content: Sandstorm's primary focus is on multiplayer, so players seeking a robust single-player experience might find it lacking in content.[/i]

In summary, Insurgency: Sandstorm is a commendable title for players craving a realistic and tactical FPS experience. Its focus on team-based strategy, immersive atmosphere, and modding support contribute to its allure, despite some technical shortcomings and a steep learning curve. For FPS enthusiasts seeking a challenging and immersive combat experience, Sandstorm is worth exploring.[/b]
